children: Kuwait has enacted a government sukuk law that will allow Islamic debt instruments to form part of its sovereign financing framework.

Kuwait's new sukuk law could broaden access to sharia-compliant funding and accelerate the development of the country's debt capital market by attracting Islamic banks and investors, Fitch Ratings said.
Islamic banks accounted for around 51% of Kuwait's banking sector assets as of end-July 2026, providing a significant potential investor base for future sovereign sukuk issuances.
Kuwait's debt capital market expanded by nearly 60% year-on-year to $52 billion at the end of H1 2026, while outstanding sukuk stood at $9.2 billion, representing 18% of the market.

According to Fitch, the 2025 financing and liquidity law, which authorises up to KWD30 billion ($100 billion) in borrowing, has helped drive market growth, with government debt rising to 15% of GDP in FY2025/26 from 3% a year earlier.
(Writing by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Kuwait’s sovereign sukuk law could accelerate debt market growth
